author_or_org: XinQi Wang, Jinwei Xiao, Sijia Cui, Hongming Zhang, Yanna Wang, Qingyang Zhang, Bo Xu

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: HyMem is a hierarchical framework that separates an agent's context into distinct functional layers, organizing context by function to separate high-level planning from execution and complex analysis.
claims.quote: To address this challenge, we propose HyMem, a hierarchical framework that explicitly separates the agent's context into distinct functional layers. HyMem organizes context by function to separate high-level planning from execution and complex analysis.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: HyMem uses an isolated reasoning module that handles complex subtasks without adding intermediate reasoning traces to the persistent planning context, and a memory management module that preserves task progress across context refreshes through structured summaries.
claims.quote: Its isolated reasoning module handles complex subtasks without adding intermediate reasoning traces to the persistent planning context, while its memory management module preserves task progress across context refreshes through structured summaries.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On GAIA and Browsecomp-plus with DeepSeek-V4, HyMem achieves average Pass@1 scores of 66.7% and 61.3%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.1 and 4.7 percentage points, respectively.
claims.quote: Experiments on GAIA and Browsecomp-plus show that, with DeepSeek-V4, HyMem achieves average Pass@1 scores of 66.7% and 61.3%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.1 and 4.7 percentage points, respectively.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Existing methods address context problems through compression or retrieval on a single, flat context, which does not clearly separate different types of context information and often leads to degraded reasoning.
claims.quote: Most existing methods address this issue through compression or retrieval applied to a single, flat context, which does not clearly separate different types of context information and often leads to degraded reasoning.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: LLM agents often perform poorly on complex, long-horizon tasks because their context becomes increasingly cluttered over time.
claims.quote: Large language model (LLM) agents often perform poorly on complex, long-horizon tasks because their context becomes increasingly cluttered over time.
